entries.name: Ember Tetra
entries.origin: Rio Araguaia basin, Goiás state, Brazil
entries.excerpt: A tiny, glowing orange tetra that adds brilliant color to nano and planted tanks. Peaceful and hardy, best kept in a group of 8 or more.
entries.schooling: School of 8 or more.

entries.name: Black Neon Tetra
entries.excerpt: A calm, hardy tetra with a bold neon stripe contrasting a dark body. Ideal for peaceful community tanks.
entries.schooling: School of 6 or more.

entries.name: Emperor Tetra
entries.origin: Río Calima and San Juan basins, western Colombia
entries.excerpt: A striking tetra with an extended, three-pronged tail in males. Males establish mild territories, so a roomy, planted tank suits them best.
entries.schooling: School of 6 or more; one male per 3 females if breeding.

entries.name: Serpae Tetra
entries.origin: Amazon and Guaporé basins, Guyana, Peru, Brazil
entries.excerpt: A vivid red tetra that may nip fins unless kept in a large group of at least 12. Very active and hardy once settled.
entries.schooling: School of 12 or more to prevent fin nipping.

entries.name: Congo Tetra
entries.origin: Congo River basin, Democratic Republic of Congo
entries.excerpt: A large, shimmering tetra with rainbow reflections on mature males. Needs a spacious tank and a shoal to display its best colors.
entries.schooling: School of 6 or more; males grow to 8 cm, females to 6 cm.

entries.name: Lemon Tetra
entries.origin: Amazon basin, Brazil (Tapajós and Xingu regions)
entries.excerpt: A gentle, schooling tetra with translucent yellow fins and lemon-tinted body. Great for planted community aquariums.
entries.schooling: School of 6 or more.

entries.name: Black Phantom Tetra
entries.origin: Río Paraguay basin, Brazil and Paraguay
entries.excerpt: A graceful dark tetra with elegant fins; males flare their dorsal in display. Hardy and perfect for peaceful planted tanks.
entries.schooling: School of 6 or more.

entries.name: Southern Platy
entries.excerpt: A friendly, colorful livebearer that adapts to almost any community tank. Extremely easy to keep and breed.
entries.schooling: Best in groups with more females than males.

entries.name: Short-finned Molly
entries.origin: Coastal rivers from Mexico to Venezuela
entries.excerpt: A versatile livebearer that tolerates hard, even brackish water. Males reach 8 cm while females can grow to 12 cm.
entries.schooling: Best in groups with more females than males.

entries.name: Endler's Livebearer
entries.excerpt: A tiny, dazzling livebearer closely related to the guppy. Avoid keeping it with guppies, as the two species hybridize freely.
entries.schooling: Best in groups; do not mix with guppies (hybridization).

entries.name: Bronze Corydoras
entries.origin: Trinidad and northern South America (widely distributed)
entries.excerpt: One of the hardiest and most popular catfish for community tanks. Forages the substrate in groups; sand is the ideal substrate.
entries.schooling: Group of 6 or more; soft sand substrate recommended.

entries.name: Panda Corydoras
entries.excerpt: A beloved black-and-white Cory that prefers cooler water than most tropical fish. Peaceful and perfect for planted tanks.
entries.schooling: Group of 6 or more.

entries.name: Three-Lined Corydoras
entries.origin: Upper Amazon tributaries, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil
entries.excerpt: Most 'Julii Cory' sold in stores are actually this species. A lovely shoaling catfish with three dark lines along the flanks.
entries.schooling: Group of 6 or more; true C. julii is rare in the trade.

entries.name: Glass Catfish
entries.excerpt: A truly transparent catfish that is shy unless kept in a group of 6 or more. Needs gentle flow and a dimly lit, mature tank.
entries.schooling: Group of 6 or more; never kept singly.

entries.name: Kribensis
entries.excerpt: A beautiful West African dwarf cichlid and one of the best beginner cichlids. Provide caves; pairs become territorial when breeding.
entries.schooling: Keep as a bonded pair; very territorial when spawning.

entries.name: Blue Acara
entries.origin: Northern South America, Venezuela, Colombia, Trinidad
entries.excerpt: A striking blue-scaled cichlid that is relatively peaceful for its size, though territorial when breeding. An avid digger, so anchor plants well.
entries.schooling: Best kept as a mated pair.

entries.name: Bolivian Ram
entries.origin: Mamoré and Guaporé drainages, Bolivia and Brazil
entries.excerpt: A hardy, peaceful dwarf cichlid that sifts sand for food. More tolerant of cooler water and varied chemistry than the Blue Ram.
entries.schooling: Pairs or groups of 6 or more in a roomy tank.

entries.name: Electric Yellow Cichlid
entries.excerpt: The famous yellow 'Yellow Lab' from Lake Malawi. One of the most peaceful mbuna; keep one male with several females.
entries.schooling: Harem of 1 male with 3 or more females.

entries.name: Firemouth Cichlid
entries.origin: Central America, Mexico to Guatemala and Belize
entries.excerpt: Named for the fiery red throat it flares during display. Robust and adaptable, but an avid digger — use sand and anchored decor.
entries.schooling: Keep as a pair in a roomy tank.

entries.name: Pearl Gourami
entries.excerpt: A peaceful labyrinth fish dusted with pearl-like spots. Adaptable to varied water, but enjoys floating plants and gentle filtration.
entries.schooling: Pairs or small groups of one male per two females.

entries.name: Three-Spot Gourami
entries.excerpt: The hardy 'Blue Gourami', available in many color morphs. Males can be aggressive with each other; a good snail-control fish.
entries.schooling: Pairs or trio of one male with two or three females.

entries.name: Sparkling Gourami
entries.origin: Mekong and Chao Phraya basins, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam
entries.excerpt: A tiny croaking gourami that fits nano planted tanks. Excellent jumper — a tight lid and floating plants are essential.
entries.schooling: Group of 4 or more.

entries.name: Tiger Barb
entries.excerpt: An iconic striped barb with a reputation for fin nipping — avoid it with long-finned fish unless kept in a group of 8 or more.
entries.schooling: Group of 8 or more; fin nipping stops in larger schools.

entries.name: Rosy Barb
entries.excerpt: A hardy, active barb that tolerates cooler water and is even kept as a pond fish in mild climates. Best in schools of 5 or more.
entries.schooling: School of 5 or more.

entries.name: Odessa Barb
entries.excerpt: A small, strikingly striped barb with a red-gold blaze. Peaceful and ideal for planted community aquariums.
entries.schooling: School of 6 or more.

entries.name: Lambchop Rasbora
entries.excerpt: A small, peaceful rasbora with a copper-orange body and a lambchop-shaped black patch. Perfect for nano planted tanks.
entries.schooling: School of 8 or more.

entries.name: Emerald Dwarf Rasbora
entries.excerpt: Not a true rasbora but a small danio from the cool, alkaline waters of Lake Inle. Unusual for a nano fish: it needs neutral-to-alkaline water.
entries.schooling: School of 8 or more; shy in smaller groups.

entries.name: Dwarf Neon Rainbowfish
entries.origin: Mamberamo River basin, West Papua, Indonesia
entries.excerpt: A vivid blue-and-red rainbowfish that stays small. Active open-water swimmer — needs a longer tank and a shoal of at least 8.
entries.schooling: School of at least 8.

entries.name: Golden Wonder Killifish
entries.excerpt: A surface-hunting killifish with golden flanks and red fins. Not annual, quite hardy, but will eat any fish small enough to fit its mouth.
entries.schooling: Singly, in pairs, or a small group in a roomy tank.

entries.name: Zebra Loach
entries.excerpt: A beautiful black-and-gold loach that lives for a decade or more. Needs sand substrate to protect its barbels and a group of 5 or more.
entries.schooling: Group of 5 or more, preferably 10.
